evals.prompt: Grill this plan: we're going to replace our REST API with GraphQL across all services in a single sprint.
evals.expected_output: Starts with checkpoint question (What problem are we solving exactly?). One question per turn. Grounds challenge in evidence (code reality, existing service boundaries). Does not dump multiple questions.
assertions: First response contains exactly one targeted question
Does not provide multiple questions in first turn
Waits for user response before continuing

evals.prompt: Challenge my assumptions about this migration plan.
evals.expected_output: Asks one scoping question to identify the plan/decision to grill. Does not start grilling without knowing the target.
assertions: Asks scoping question about which plan/decision to grill
Does not start assumption-challenging without clear target

evals.prompt: Grill me on this: we're adding a caching layer with Redis. Rollback is to just turn off Redis and fall back to direct DB queries.
evals.expected_output: Deep-dive triggered (rollback path + expensive-to-reverse decision). Challenges rollback claim with specifics (cache invalidation, data consistency during transition, latency impact). Uses terse format (Question + Why + Wait).
assertions: Challenges the simplicity of the rollback claim
Output uses terse format (Question + Why this matters + Wait)
Does not accept rollback plan at face value

evals.prompt:
Grill me on this plan. Then update the ADR with the decision.

Plan: migrate user auth from session cookies to JWT tokens.
evals.expected_output: Runs grilling interview first. When ADR update is requested, proposes it as explicit follow-up action requiring execution approval. Does not edit docs during grilling session.
assertions: Starts grilling interview, not doc editing
ADR update is proposed as follow-up requiring execution approval
Does not edit docs during the grilling session
Grilling includes at least one checkpoint question about the auth migration

evals.prompt:
Grill me on our API design. The endpoint accepts a 'user' parameter.

CONTEXT.md says 'user' means account holder. The code uses 'user' for both account holders and admin users.
evals.expected_output: Detects domain term conflict between CONTEXT.md and code. Challenges fuzzy term immediately. Asks user to choose authoritative source. Does not proceed with ambiguous terminology.
assertions: Detects 'user' term conflict between CONTEXT.md and code
Asks user to choose authoritative definition
Does not proceed with ambiguous term
